title: Dark color palette that stays readable
when: The user wants a dark look or dark theme colors and needs surfaces, text and accents that read well without glare.
inputs: the light palette or brand color, if any
dark only, or dark next to light
prompt:
Goal: A dark palette of layered gray surfaces, softened text and desaturated accents that passes AA on every surface level.
Steps:
1. Start the base at a dark gray (#121212 to #1a1b1e), not pure black, so layers still show.
2. Show elevation by lightness: each raised surface (card, menu, dialog) is 4 to 8 percent lighter than the one below.
3. Use off white body text (around #e6e6e6) and a secondary gray that passes 4.5 to 1 on the lightest surface.
4. Lower accent saturation by 10 to 20 points so it does not vibrate, then retest the label on it.
5. Separate surfaces with a 1 px border one step lighter; drop shadows barely show on dark.
6. Put tokens under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) or [data-theme="dark"] with color-scheme: dark so native controls match.
Quality bar:
- Body text between 7 and 15 to 1.
- Every surface level has a passing text color.
- Photos are never inverted.
Pitfalls:
- Saturated blue on near black, which blurs.
- Checking text only on the base surface.
- Forgetting color-scheme, so inputs stay light.
Verify:
- [ ] A dark rule holds the dark tokens.
- [ ] Surface steps are ordered.
- [ ] Every text pair passes 4.5 to 1.
- [ ] color-scheme: dark is set.
Output: The dark token block in style.css beside the light one, with the same token names.

examples.input: paleta escura para um app de notas
examples.output: bg #16171a, surface-1 #1f2024, surface-2 #2a2b30, text #e8e6e3, accent #7aa7e0 desaturated
